title: = I36a: Bundle I's extraction and acquisition, no laws: the message queue, the messenger, the whitelist and the Submitter extracted at the pinned head (overloads, dynamic storage arrays, abi.encodeWithSignature and encodeCall, packed hashing over loop-carried values) and modelled, one linked machine in which calls between members run the callee's extracted transitions, refined against a forge harness of the real bundle, and the legacy registry L1Staking extracted at v0.6.1 with its proxy's on-chain implementation matched by metadata-stripped bytecode (Q12), the live members matched to their head builds (Q18)

predictions.claim: The legacy registry is recovered (Q12), decided on tests_m3/_i69.py::timeline's recomputation from the committed snapshot's raw logs, receipts and code (rules A3-A6: each upgrade rebuilt from the proxy's raw Upgraded logs, confirmed by its committed receipt, the proxy addresses the sidecar's, the scan's end anchored by the EIP-1967 implementation slot at the fetch block), and UNKNOWN (neither held nor missed) when the anchor test test_the_second_read_agrees (A7) fails: the registry proxy 0x0dc417f8af88388737c5053ff73f345f080543f7 (the old registry of I63's cutover receipt) has exactly two Upgraded logs in the window [19426587, 26179508]. The first is in its creation transaction: the receipt's contractAddress is the proxy, its implementation is I63's placeholder 0x98df320641c2e65ab4bbef1e6f6c66d9b50ede5f, its sender is the Rollup proxy's deployer 0x2818a3af785975a32611155a6ee36c21cec068ca, and it logs one AdminChanged (from zero to that sender), no Initialized and matches nothing. The second, before the cutover block 26031669, sets an implementation that matches the registry's version V3 (the 22 tags v0.4.0..v0.6.1) under the hardhat configuration alone, logs Initialized(1) in its transaction, and holds at its immutables OTHER_STAKING = 0x5300000000000000000000000000000000000015 (the L2 staking predeploy) and MESSENGER = the MESSENGER word of the queue proxy's last implementation. Derivation: Morph's deploy scripts create every proxy over one placeholder from one deployer (I63 saw it for the Rollup proxy at block 20996846); L1Staking's code is one identity across all 22 tags of the mainnet era under every configuration (the basis), so nothing called for an upgrade after launch; every pre-cutover Rollup implementation matched under hardhat alone (I63's timeline), so the launch-era pipeline is hardhat's; the legacy registry was built against the same L1 messenger proxy as the queue. Disclosed: OTHER_STAKING's value follows from the constructor, which passes Predeploys.L2_STAKING (L1Staking.sol:93 at v0.6.1), read before the prereg; the on-chain word is still read, since the code identity masks immutables.

The live bundle is the modelled code (Q18's cross-check for the members), decided on the instrument's timeline (A6; UNKNOWN when the A7 anchor test fails): the last implementation in the window of the queue proxy 0x3931ade842f5bb8763164bdd81e5361dce6cc1ef (the receiver of the Rollup's IL1MessageQueue calls in I23's record) matches the queue's head build under hardhat alone, with ROLLUP_CONTRACT = the Rollup proxy 0x759894ced0e6af42c26668076ffa84d02e3cef60; the messenger proxy (the low 20 bytes of the queue's MESSENGER word) has a last implementation that matches the messenger's head build under hardhat alone; the Submitter proxy 0xf2d50000c994565a4742059802fdbb0bee1cbef6 (the new registry of I63's cutover receipt) has a last implementation that matches the Submitter's head build under deployed alone; and the whitelist the queue names at the fetch block (the low 20 bytes of its word at the whitelistChecker slot) matches the Whitelist's head build under hardhat and foundry (whose builds are equal) and not under deployed. Derivation: the head's L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle.sol is the blob of every tag from v0.4.10 on, its L1CrossDomainMessenger.sol the blob from v0.4.2 on and its Whitelist.sol the blob of every tag (git ls-tree, no blob read), all released in the hardhat era (I63: every Rollup implementation before the cutover matched under hardhat); Submitter.sol first appears at v0.6.3, the cutover's version, whose Rollup implementation matched under deployed alone.

Five documents and their coverage (E1-E5): holon bundle extract declares five documents (messenger, queue, whitelist and Submitter at the head; L1Staking at v0.6.1) with no member debt; the declaration's coverage gives each no unaccounted statement and exactly the debt entries of thresholds.debt (messenger 18: the queue calls at :198, :208, :209, :286, :290, :298 and :320, IRollup.withdrawalRoots at :147, and the low-level transfers at :161, :203, :240, :293 and :313, each an external_call and a value_transfer; queue 1: IWhitelist.isSenderAllowed at :115; whitelist 1: the loop writing isWhitelisted at :25-28; Submitter 4: the getters at :134 and :172 and the transfer at :178; L1Staking 10: six storage-writing loops, the transfer at :467 and the two ICrossDomainMessenger.sendMessage_b2267a7b calls at :475-480 and :486-491); and holon coverage --milestone M3 lists the four head documents with the declaration's entries beside the unchanged Rollup entry, with no unaccounted statement in all. Derivation: reading the sources under I19's coverage rules, which make every external call, value transfer and storage-writing loop debt at its site; every other statement is a construct the build's extensions extract, so none is unsupported.

The documents are as read (thresholds.structure's loops and cost): per document, the loop records per action and the loop spans of the cost terms per action. Derivation: reading the sources, most derived first, by I19's rules; for example the queue's Yul length loop (:154-157) is recorded at each of its 5 or 6 uses with one cost span, and L1Staking.slash holds its own storage-writing loop and getStakersFromBitmap's two counting loops. The action names (E2's sendMessage_b2267a7b and sendMessage_5f7b1577; 16 messenger, 17 queue, 4 whitelist, 15 Submitter and 27 L1Staking actions), the own storage families, the inherited entries (13, 5, 1, 7 and L1Staking's 7) and the constants (the queue's APPROPRIATE_INTRINSIC_GAS_PER_BYTE 16 and INTRINSIC_GAS_TX 21000; none elsewhere) are construction facts of solc's AST and layout, checked under I69-R5 (the prereg review's m1), not predicted.

Member models (M1-M4): holon bundle model compiles the four head members' documents with no model debt, and on every top-level corpus step on its member each model agrees with the real code (status, the revert key on two reverts, the return data on two oks, the member's storage at every slot a write of the step touches on either side, and its logs) from the member's real pre-state with the recorded answers to its own calls: no disagreement and no unsupported step. Derivation: the extensions M1 and M2 name cover every construct the four documents hold, as read; a disagreement would be an extraction or model error.

The linked machine refines the bundle (L1-L8, C1-C6): the declaration's static links are the 28 rows of thresholds.links (Rollup 12, messenger 11, Submitter 4, queue 1; 22 to actions, 5 to getters, 1 to the Rollup's receive), of which the 16 rows of the messenger, the queue and the Submitter are predicted by reading and the Rollup's 12 are rule L2 on the committed adopted document (construction, reproduced by the review); and on the whole corpus (300 m1, 7 seed and 120 random traces) the linked machine agrees with the real bundle in every observable (status, revert key, return data, every member's storage at every touched slot, logs, balances, outgoing calls) and in its frames (C2's form, equal to the harness's): no disagreement and no unsupported step, in the record and in every compared step of results/M3/bundle/steps.json. Derivation: the members' call graph has no writing re-entry (messenger to queue to whitelist and the Rollup to queue and Submitter call down only; the Submitter calls the Rollup's getters and its empty receive), so L5 never refuses a step of the corpus.

The corpus reaches every link and action, decided on tests_m3/_i69.py::recount of the harness's frames in results/M3/bundle/steps.json (C6), with the record's frames_ok, links_ok and by_member_action equal to the recount: each of the 28 link rows is executed with a kept frame (C2's ok) at least once, and each action of the four head members that is not an initializer (49 by rule E2, a construction count: 15 messenger, 16 queue, 4 whitelist, 14 Submitter) ends ok in at least one kept frame, top-level or nested. Derivation: the seven planted traces call each action past its guards as read (fees, the whitelist, the poked withdrawal root, the gateway caller, the Rollup as caller, a won challenge), and I20's m1 rows drive the Rollup's calls into the queue and the Submitter.

I69's own commits (the contract's one-PR definition: the non-merge commits of git log --first-parent <C_K>..<end>, end the oldest commit adding docs/iterations/I69.md, HEAD while none does; shown on toy repositories in docs/iterations/I69_prereg_fold.json) change only what the contract allows: at least one adds gen/M3/bundle/bundle.json; none changes a frozen root, laws/, spec/ (but lines of iteration I69 appended to spec/M3/amendments.jsonl), holon/rules/, a file under replay/ outside replay/M3/bundle/, a file under gen/ outside gen/M3/bundle/ but gen/M3/coverage.json (whose entries at the commit's parent stay as they are), or a file under results/ outside results/M3/bundle/ but the records directly under results/M1, results/M2 and results/T32, none of which it adds or deletes, each keeping its status and differing from its parent's version only in generator_sha256 and keys named seconds (so I40's filter stage is re-applied in the same commit, and the lean4 kernel entries rebuild as they are). No M3 record is re-made: every M3 record's generator_sha256 trails I69's closures (GEN3, GEN_FACT, GEN_UNDO, GEN_DISCH, holon-ir/0.3) until the next M3 re-make. These rules imply I63-R2, I43-R8, I26-R1, I31-R2 and I40-R2 for I69's commits.

On the build head: holon coverage --milestone M3 --check reproduces the committed report (G8's reproduction, over the four head documents) and holon audit prereg exits 0 for M3 and M2 (checked by the test); in CI on the PR, every job that passed at the base (run 40116936084 on 2ef07b6d: all 11 jobs, gate-M0, gate-M1, gate-M2 in full, gate-M3-partial --checks G3,G5,G8,G9,G10,G11,G11V,GEVID with G8 covering the four head documents, gate-M3-G2, tests-m3-catalog, the frozen suite, freeze-check, prereg-M2, prereg-M3 and the toolchain) passes, and a job fails only on an item it fails on at the lead the branch last merged (after I28's build: G11V's 'in-flight: 0 of 8 edges inhabited'), I69 adding none, save G8 on a head document if I69-P3 misses by an unaccounted statement (P3's miss, not counted again). The full M3 gate is not claimed: its G1 fails on the M3 records' staleness until the next M3 re-make, as after I66.
